\begin{tablenotes}[flushleft]
\footnotesize
\item \textit{Notes:} Dates are interval-end dates (ET); Obs.\ and the rolling estimation window $W$ are in the units of each panel. The burn-in is the longest HAR horizon, \rhdmBurnIn{} observations of each series as built: on the closing-interval series, one observation a trading day, \rhdmBurnInDaysClose{} trading days, so the closing-interval sample starts in 2010; on the series of the two intervals of the last hour (the linear pre-sample) \rhdmBurnInDaysPre{} trading days, so the pre-sample starts in 2004; on the intraday grid (Panel B) \rhdmBurnIn{} 30-minute intervals, \rhdmBurnInDaysGrid{} trading days. The trees and the pooled linear models of Table~\ref{tab:rh_oos} and Sections~\ref{sec:rh_results}--\ref{sec:rh_econ} are re-estimated at every bar on the previous 39{,}000 regular-hours bars (3{,}000 trading days of 13 bars); the pooled linear models on all \rhdmNIntervals{} intervals (in the model set) use $W = \rhdmPooledLinWindow$ intervals (\cmPtFitWin{} trading days). The tree hyperparameters are chosen once, by an Optuna search on the 1998--2002 development sample that fits each candidate on the previous 24{,}000 intervals and scores it on the next 250, stepping forward 250 intervals at a time. Each validation sample follows a 25-day gap and a \cmPtFitWin-day estimation sample (Section~\ref{sec:rh_exp_samples}). The penalties of the pooled linear models on the regular-hours bars are chosen once, on pre-sample fold \rhdmPlPreFoldUsed: each candidate is fitted on the $W$ bars before a gap of \rhdmPlPreEmbargoSess{} sessions (\rhdmPlPreEmbargoBars{} bars) and scored on the next \rhdmPlPreFoldSess{} sessions (\rhdmPlPreFoldBars{} bars, the validation row above); a penalty selected at an end of its grid adds the next decade in that direction until the selection is interior, stopping when the criterion changes by less than \rhdmPlGridExtTol{} relative or after \rhdmPlGridExtCap{} decades. Full trading days: expiration days that are not early-close days. Panel C: the evaluation span holds every trading day on which all rolling forecasts exist (Section~\ref{sec:rh_results_eval}); the straddle economics use its option-data subsample (Section~\ref{sec:rh_econ}).
\end{tablenotes}
